title: showreel accepts an output pattern whose names it cannot keep apart, one naming a directory, one with the counter in the last extension, or one ending in a video's extension, and check calls such a reel valid
body:
## What

`deliver::stem` builds a revision's name from the reel's `output:` pattern, and it accepts three shapes of pattern that name files showreel cannot keep apart. `showreel check`, which never builds the stem, calls a reel with any of them valid.

- **A pattern that names a directory.** `stem` fills the pattern's fields with values that `tight` keeps to letters and digits, and the date's digits, but it keeps the pattern's own literal text as written, path separators included. So `output: 'sub/{nnn}.html'` or `'../{nnn}.html'` names a file outside `_out/` itself, which `revisions` never counts, since it lists `_out/` alone. On main every build named 001 again and replaced it. Since 0098 every build after the first refuses, because the file is there, and that refusal's remedy (build again, or move the file aside) sends a user round in circles. An absolute pattern (`/x/{nnn}.html`) writes wherever it names, since joining an absolute path replaces the base. A fixed name of `..`, `.` or nothing names a directory with no `/` in it, `_out/`'s parent or `_out/` itself, and the build fails at the write with the system's words (`Is a directory`) and the remedy `check the path`, which names neither the pattern nor the fix.
- **A pattern whose counter is in the name's last extension**, eg `output: '{date}.{nnn}'`. `video_of` names a revision's video by replacing the name's last extension with the container's, and here that extension holds the counter, so every revision's video takes the same name (`20260919.mp4`). On main each recording replaced the one before with nothing said, and `prune` took the newest video with the oldest revision, since every slot names the same video. Under 0100, which refuses a slot whose video name is taken, every build after the first recording refuses on it.
- **A pattern whose last extension is a video container's**, eg `output: '{date}-{nnn}.mp4'`, a fixed `reel.mp4`, or `{nnn}.MOV`, since APFS does not tell case apart by default. A revision's videos take its name with the last extension replaced by `mp4` or `mov`, so the HTML takes one of its own videos' names. On main `video` replaced an `.mp4` HTML with the recording, since a slot's video is always `.mp4`, and `prune` listed the HTML twice, as itself and as its video, so a build with `--keep` fails at the second removal, after the first. Under 0100 a counted `.mp4` one records and then refuses at `place`, naming its own HTML as the file at the video's name.
- **`check` calls such a reel valid.** `showreel check` runs `build::open`, the opener both verbs call, and says the reel is valid; `open` neither stamps the date nor builds the stem, which `build::run` alone does. So `check` passes a reel whose `output:` `build` refuses (two counters, an unclosed or an unknown field, and each shape above), and one whose date `build` refuses (an `iso:` that is not a date).

critic-rust found the first reading 0098's candidate v1 on 22 Oct 2026, and the second reading 0100's candidate v1 the same day. cc found the third and `check`'s drafting this issue's first amendment the same day, and vc found the third reading it. vc made the first cc's own issue, low, for 2.14.2 after 0100 (22 Oct), refused by name where the stem is built. On the critic reads (22 Oct), vc added the fixed `..`, `.` and empty names and folded in the second shape; on its read of that amendment (22 Oct), it folded in the third and `check`'s, since hv's rule stacks everything outstanding into the next release, they are the same family, and one landing with one set of runs saves host time.

## Where, by reading (main at `020fd4db`)

- **The stem**: `stem` (`deliver.rs:230-318`) puts the literal text before each field into the prefix or the suffix as written (`:280`), and the text after the last field into the suffix (`:307`) or the fixed name (`:314`).
- **The name**: `Stem::next` joins it onto `_out/` (`:220` for a fixed name, `:223` for a counted one).
- **The video's name**: `video_of` (`:327`) is the revision's name with its last extension replaced by the container's (`Path::with_extension`), for `video`, which records to it (`video.rs:116`), and `slot_files` (`:335`), which prunes it with its revision.
- **The opener**: `build::open` (`build.rs:49`) resolves everything a verb needs from a reel, and its doc says why it is one home: `check` exists to resolve exactly what `build` resolves. `check` (`main.rs:112`) calls it and nothing else before it says the reel is valid. `run` stamps the date (`build.rs:218`) and builds the stem (`:254`) itself.

## Design

cc, 22 Oct 2026, at `020fd4db`. Size: S. It lands after 0100 and is built on 0100's landing. Read and approved by vc, 22 Oct, as it stands. Amended on vc's ruling of 22 Oct on the critic reads of candidate v1 and of 0100's: a fixed `..`, `.` or empty name is refused as a directory (point 1), and the counter in the name's last extension in its own words (point 2). Amended again on vc's read of that amendment (22 Oct): a video container's extension (point 3) and `check` (point 4), each with its own test (point 5). Amended a third time on vc's read of the second (22 Oct): point 5 (d) tests the date's refusal as well as the stem's, and point 4 names what is read rather than tested.

1. **A pattern that names a directory is refused by name, where the stem is built.** Once `stem` has assembled the stem, it refuses a name holding `/` (a counted stem's prefix or suffix, or a fixed name), the one separator on the platforms showreel runs on: `output pattern names a directory: '<pattern>'`, with the remedy `the pattern names a file in _out/; take the / out`. It refuses an absolute pattern too. It refuses a fixed name that is empty, `.` or `..` in the same words, with the remedy `the pattern names a file in _out/; give it a name, eg reel.html`. The pattern is quoted, so an empty one shows as `''`. v1 checked the pattern's own text, which relied on the fields holding no `/` (`tight` keeps letters and digits, and the date is digits); the assembled names need no such reliance, and every check of the names then sits in one function, which points 2 and 3 share (critic-rust's note on v1). `write`'s comment, which gives such a pattern as one way a file can already be at a revision's name, says it is refused since 0101.
2. **A pattern whose counter is in the name's last extension is refused in its own words, where the stem is built.** For a counted stem, `stem` names revisions 001 and 002 and asks `video_of` for each one's video. When the two are the same, the counter is in the extension `video_of` replaces, so every revision's video would take that one name: `output pattern gives every revision's video the same name: '<pattern>'`, with the remedy `a video takes its revision's name with the last extension replaced, and here that extension holds the counter; end the pattern with an extension after it, eg {date}-{nnn}.html`. Two revisions settle it, since the counter is wholly inside the last extension or wholly outside it. The check asks `video_of` itself, so it holds whatever `video_of` does, and it needs no rule of its own for which dot starts an extension (a name that begins with its only dot has none). A revision's name gets one home, which `Stem::next` and these checks use.
3. **A pattern whose last extension is a video container's is refused in its own words, where the stem is built**, counted and fixed alike. When the name revision 001 takes, or the fixed name, is one of its own videos' names, `stem` refuses: `output pattern gives the HTML a video's extension: '<pattern>'`, with the remedy `a revision's videos take its name with the last extension replaced by mp4 or mov, so this HTML would take one of its own videos' names; end the pattern with .html`. It asks `video_of` for each of `VIDEO_EXTENSIONS`, as point 2 asks it, and compares the two names without case, since APFS does not tell case apart by default; point 2 compares through the same function. A fixed `reel.mp4` had its HTML replaced by its own recording each time, which reads as working when only `video` is run; it is refused too, since an HTML named as a video is never what a reel means, and `-o` is how a video is named. Every refusal of points 1 to 3 refuses a build with `--out` too, as the pattern's other refusals do, since the stem is built before `--out` is read: the reel's own `output:` is wrong whatever one build's destination.
4. **`check` refuses what `build` refuses.** `build::open`, the opener both verbs call, stamps the session's date (`deliver::stamp`) and builds the stem (`deliver::stem`), and `Opened` carries the stem and the stamp's warnings. `run` takes both from it and drains the warnings into `said` where it drains them now, after the socials', so what a build says, and in what order, is unchanged; its refusals of the stem and the date now come before the payload and the render, since `open` runs first. `check` then refuses with `build`'s words and exit (a refusal, exit 2) every pattern refusal (two counters, an unclosed or an unknown field, and points 1 to 3) and a date that `stamp` refuses, and it says the stamp's warnings on stderr as `build` does, since a warning returned and never said is silent. That last is read rather than tested: `check` lives in `main.rs`, which holds no tests, by the crate's own rule (`lib.rs`).
5. **Red first.** (a) Beside `a_pattern_with_two_counters_is_refused_with_the_pattern_named` (`deliver.rs:586`), `a_pattern_that_names_a_directory_is_refused_by_name_issue_0101`: `sub/{nnn}.html`, `../{nnn}.html`, `/tmp/{nnn}.html`, and the fixed `sub/reel.html`, `..`, `.` and `''`, each refuse, naming the pattern. Red by a one-line mutation for each check: the `/` check taken out, and the fixed name's. 0098's `write_next` test builds `Stem::Counted` with the prefix `sub/r-` directly, which stays right (vc). (b) Point 2's own test: `{date}.{nnn}` and `r.{nnn}x` refuse in point 2's words, naming the pattern; `{date}.{nnn}.html`, `{nnn}` (no extension, so the video's name adds one) and `.{nnn}` (a name that begins with its only dot has no extension either) build. Red by a one-line mutation that takes the check out. (c) Point 3's own test: `{date}-{nnn}.mp4`, a fixed `reel.mp4` and `{nnn}.MOV` refuse in point 3's words, naming the pattern; `{date}-{nnn}.mp4.html` builds, since only the last extension counts. Red by a one-line mutation that takes the check out. (d) Point 4's own test, in `build.rs` beside the opener's other tests: `open`, which is all `check` runs before it says a reel is valid, refuses a reel with two counters and a reel with point 2's shape, each in `stem`'s words, and a reel whose `iso:` is not a date, in `stamp`'s words, each with exit 2. Red by a one-line mutation in `open` for each of its two refusals: one that skips the stem's, and one that skips the stamp's. The test is on `open` because `main.rs` holds no tests, by the crate's own rule (`lib.rs`).
6. **Runs**, each booked with utilz-vc. The candidate is built in its own worktree under `~/Devel/scratch/utilz-cc/`. R (heavy): the tests' six mutations. G (heavy): `bin/utilz test prez` under an empty TMPDIR of the run's own, then `bin/devbin check all`. K: utilz-dc's kovacs leg, `cargo test --release --workspace --no-fail-fast` on the same bytes.
7. **Versions and CHANGELOG.** prez 2.5.9, after 0100's 2.5.8, one bump per landing. One line under 2.14.2's Fixed, after 0100's, naming the three shapes and `check`, added at the landing.
